title: Lactate trajectories and clinical outcomes
summary: Candidate design coordinates for repeated-lactate trajectory or clearance studies. Sampling is treatment- and severity-dependent, so measurement intensity, landmark timing, and immortal-time risk must be handled explicitly.

design_candidates.population: ICU patients with enough temporally ordered lactate observations for the declared trajectory or landmark analysis.
design_candidates.time_zero: ICU admission, shock recognition, or first qualifying lactate; select one landmark before deriving exposure trajectories.
design_candidates.observation_window: A fixed early window for lactate measurements and treatments, with sampling density reported.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: Outcomes begin after trajectory classification or use a correctly specified time-varying analysis.
eligibility_candidates: Specify minimum observations without conditioning on future survival
design_candidates.exposure: Baseline lactate, prespecified change or clearance, or a validated longitudinal trajectory assignment.
design_candidates.outcome: Mortality or organ-support outcome beginning after exposure ascertainment, with horizon and censoring defined.
design_candidates.estimand: Outcome contrast across prespecified lactate patterns in patients observable at the selected landmark.
recommended_methods: Adjustment for baseline severity and measurement process
sensitivity_analyses: Adjustment or stratification by lactate sampling intensity

stop_conditions: Lactate timestamps or units cannot be harmonized
Trajectory exposure uses measurements occurring after outcome follow-up begins
Selected sampling requirements induce unquantifiable survivor bias
requires_confirmation: Confirm whether the exposure is baseline lactate, change, clearance, or a longitudinal trajectory
Confirm the landmark and the minimum measurement support without conditioning on future survival
